title: High Availability, Replication and Disaster Recovery
learningObjectives: Distinguish high availability from backup and disaster recovery.
Explain primary and replica roles at a conceptual level.
Measure a recorded replication checkpoint delay.
Define recovery point and recovery time objectives.
Use restore-test records to assess recovery readiness.

understand.concept: High availability reduces service interruption, replication copies changes between database instances, and disaster recovery restores service after a major failure. They solve related but different operational problems.
understand.whyItMatters: A replica can copy accidental deletion or corruption, while a backup can be too old or untested. Reliable recovery needs multiple controls and measurable objectives.
understand.analogy: A second power source keeps a building running during an outage, while an emergency plan restores operations after the building is damaged.
understand.analogyLimit: A SQLite table that records replica checkpoints or restore tests is only a teaching model; it does not implement replication, failover or disaster recovery.

explain.narrative:
## Availability and replication
High availability aims to keep a service available during component failures. Replication maintains copies of database changes on other nodes, but replication lag and failover correctness must be monitored. Replication is not a substitute for independent backups.

## RPO and RTO
Recovery Point Objective (RPO) describes the maximum acceptable data-loss window. Recovery Time Objective (RTO) describes the target time to restore service. Both should be defined by business impact and tested during recovery exercises.

## Disaster recovery evidence
Record restore drills, measured RPO/RTO, validation outcome and responsible operator. A successful test should verify application-level data and service behaviour, not merely that a database file opened.

## Engine boundary
SQLite is an embedded database and does not provide a built-in server replication/failover cluster. Its journal/WAL and backup facilities solve different problems. PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQL Server provide product-specific replication and HA technologies that require separate configuration and operational testing.

examples.title: Create a restore-drill history table
examples.code: CREATE TABLE ops21_restore_drills (drill_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tested_at TEXT NOT NULL, restore_status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (restore_status IN ('passed','failed')), rpo_minutes INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (rpo_minutes >= 0), rto_minutes INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (rto_minutes >= 0));
examples.explanation: Stores measured recovery exercise outcomes. RPO and RTO are recorded as minutes for this teaching example; production records should also identify the recovery scope and tested backup chain.

examples.title: Record three recovery exercises
examples.explanation: Records two successful restore drills and one failed drill. A failed test should trigger corrective work and a repeat test rather than being hidden by a later successful record.

examples.title: Read the most recent recovery exercise
examples.code: SELECT tested_at, restore_status, rpo_minutes, rto_minutes FROM ops21_restore_drills ORDER BY tested_at DESC LIMIT 1;
examples.explanation: Returns the latest drill. The measured RPO is 10 minutes and RTO is 35 minutes; compare these values with approved business objectives.

examples.title: Count failed recovery exercises
examples.code: SELECT COUNT(*) AS failed_drills FROM ops21_restore_drills WHERE restore_status = 'failed';
examples.explanation: Counts failed restore exercises. An operational dashboard should alert on failures and track remediation to closure.

examples.title: Estimate replica checkpoint delay from recorded timestamps
examples.code: CREATE TABLE ops21_replica_checkpoints (replica_name TEXT PRIMARY KEY, last_applied_at TEXT NOT NULL); INSERT INTO ops21_replica_checkpoints VALUES ('replica-east', '2026-11-22T09:55:00Z'); SELECT CAST(ROUND((julianday('2026-11-22T10:00:00Z') - julianday(last_applied_at)) * 1440, 0) AS INTEGER) AS lag_minutes FROM ops21_replica_checkpoints WHERE replica_name = 'replica-east';
examples.explanation: Calculates a five-minute difference between a reference primary timestamp and a recorded replica checkpoint. This is a metadata calculation only; it does not create or monitor an actual replica and the reference timestamp must come from a trusted clock.

practise.guidedTask: Run the restore-drill examples and compare the latest RPO/RTO with a hypothetical target of 15 minutes RPO and 45 minutes RTO. Explain why the failed drill still requires remediation.
practise.independentTask: Design an HA and disaster-recovery scorecard with replica lag, last successful backup, latest restore test, RPO, RTO and unresolved failures. State which values require a real DBMS/monitoring integration.
hints: HA, replication and backup/recovery are different controls.

RPO measures acceptable data loss; RTO measures restore time.
Record and remediate failed restore tests.

options: The acceptable data-loss window
The time to display a query result
The number of database tables
The number of replica servers only
questions.explanation: RPO describes how much recent data the business can afford to lose.

options: The target time to restore service
The age of the oldest SQL lesson
The number of rows in a backup table
The delay between two SELECT statements
questions.answer: The target time to restore service
questions.explanation: RTO is the target recovery duration.

questions.prompt: Is replication a substitute for independent backups?
options: No; replicas can copy accidental deletion or corruption
Yes, always
Only in SQLite
Only when the replica is read-only
questions.answer: No; replicas can copy accidental deletion or corruption
questions.explanation: Backups provide a separate recovery path from live replication.

questions.prompt: What should happen after a failed restore drill?
options: Investigate, remediate and repeat the test
Delete the failed drill record
Increase the RPO without approval
Assume the next backup will work
questions.answer: Investigate, remediate and repeat the test
questions.explanation: Recovery failures need tracked corrective action.

questions.prompt: Does a SQLite checkpoint metadata table implement replication?
options: No; it only stores teaching metadata
Yes, it creates a replica automatically
Yes, it configures failover
Only when indexed
questions.answer: No; it only stores teaching metadata
questions.explanation: Actual replication requires engine-specific infrastructure and configuration.
